title: ADR-000: Common evaluation criteria for all tool selections
description:
Define the shared evaluation template that every ADR (001–010) will apply. Produces a reusable criteria rubric and a short prose section that each ADR includes by reference.

## Why this exists

Each ADR will evaluate different tools against different functional requirements, but a set of cross-cutting criteria applies to all of them. Defining these once avoids drift between ADRs and forces each decision to be honest about the same hard constraints.

## Budget constraint

**Budget is effectively 0€.** This is a first-class filter, not a soft preference. It means:
- Managed cloud services (Confluent Cloud, Datadog, Temporal Cloud, AWS MSK, etc.) are disqualified unless they have a genuinely usable free tier with no credit-card-required production cliff.
- Self-hosted open-source is the default mode.
- Tools with open-core models are acceptable only if the features required by the architecture sit in the free/community tier — the ADR must explicitly verify this.
- Licensing traps (BSL, SSPLv1, ELv2, Commons Clause) must be flagged even if currently free, because they constrain future use.

## Criteria to define

1. **Cost / licensing** — total cost of self-hosting (infra, ops time) vs free tier limits; licence type and change risk.
2. **Regulatory fit** — GDPR (data residency, right to erasure), DORA (resilience testing, RTO/RPO documentation), PSD2 (audit trail, SCA). Hard pass/fail before functional comparison.
3. **Operational complexity at small scale** — how much ops burden does this add to a small team? Preference for tools that degrade gracefully when not actively tuned.
4. **Ecosystem coherence** — does it compose with the rest of the chosen stack without bespoke glue? Native OpenTelemetry, standard connectors, etc.
5. **Exit cost** — how painful is migration away in 3–5 years? Does the tool own a data format or protocol that creates lock-in?
6. **Community and longevity** — is this tool likely to still be maintained in 10 years? Red flags: single-vendor control with recent licence change, stagnant commits, small contributor base.
7. **Functional fit** — tool-specific criteria defined per ADR.

## Deliverable

A markdown section titled '## Common Evaluation Criteria' usable as a template block in each ADR, plus a summary rubric table (criteria × weight) that each ADR fills in for its candidates.
acceptance_criteria: Template section written and agreed. Each ADR-001–010 issue updated to reference this template.

title: ADR series: tool selection for integration implementation
description: A conversation-driven ADR series covering every major technology decision needed to move the integration_concepts documents into working software. Each child issue drives one focused conversation and produces one ADR in markdown. Acceptance: all child ADRs written and committed.

title: ADR-010: Anti-corruption layer implementation approach
description: Decide the implementation pattern for the ACL between the domain and Core Banking (doc 02). Conversation topics: dedicated ACL service vs sidecar vs library; adapter patterns for SOAP/XML ↔ domain events; polling adapter vs webhook vs MQ bridge depending on Core capabilities; failure isolation — bulkhead and circuit-breaker placement; how ACL state interacts with the outbox (ADR-004). Deliverable: ADR-010.md in integration_concepts/adrs/.

title: ADR-009: Testing infrastructure and contract testing
description: Decide the testing tools for the strategy in doc 07 — component, integration, contract, and saga tests. Conversation topics: Pact vs OpenAPI contract testing vs schema-registry compatibility checks; Testcontainers for Kafka and DB integration tests; saga test harness — replaying events against the orchestrator in isolation; chaos/resilience testing (DORA requirement, doc 10); test data management for a GDPR-regulated system. Deliverable: ADR-009.md in integration_concepts/adrs/.

title: ADR-008: Event catalog governance tooling
description: Decide the tooling for maintaining the event catalog and schema governance described in doc 08. Conversation topics: AsyncAPI as the specification format; EventCatalog vs Backstage vs Confluent Control Center vs custom portal; ownership model and review gates tied to the schema registry (ADR-002); breaking-change detection automation; integration with CI/CD. Deliverable: ADR-008.md in integration_concepts/adrs/.

title: ADR-007: Observability stack
description: Decide the distributed tracing, metrics, and logging tools for the observability model in doc 06. Conversation topics: OpenTelemetry as the instrumentation baseline (traces, metrics, logs); Jaeger vs Tempo vs Zipkin for trace backends; Prometheus + Grafana vs Datadog vs Elastic APM; correlation of trace IDs with the identity trio (doc 01 — correlation/causation IDs); GDPR-safe logging — what can be stored and for how long (doc 10). Deliverable: ADR-007.md in integration_concepts/adrs/.

title: ADR-006: Edge API gateway and synchronous layer
description: Decide the API gateway and edge technology for the synchronous REST/JSON layer described in doc 00 (the sub-500ms boundary). Conversation topics: Kong vs AWS API Gateway vs custom BFF per channel (web/mobile/branch); how the gateway enforces PSD2 SCA (doc 10); rate limiting and circuit-breaking at the edge; SSE/WebSocket push for optimistic UI status updates; integration with the identity/auth layer. Deliverable: ADR-006.md in integration_concepts/adrs/.

title: ADR-005: CQRS read model storage
description: Decide the storage technology for the materialized read models described in doc 03. Conversation topics: PostgreSQL projections vs Elasticsearch vs Redis vs dedicated read DBs per bounded context; write throughput from event replay; query flexibility vs operational simplicity; how the ACL (doc 02) feeds Core Banking data into these projections; cache invalidation and eventual consistency UX implications. Deliverable: ADR-005.md in integration_concepts/adrs/.

title: ADR-004: Outbox pattern mechanism
description: Decide the technical mechanism for implementing the outbox pattern (doc 04 — the non-negotiable primitive for dual-write safety). Conversation topics: CDC-based outbox via Debezium vs polling publisher vs library-embedded outbox (Eventuate Tram, Axon outbox); connector reliability and lag SLAs; database compatibility (PostgreSQL assumed); interaction with idempotency and inbox deduplication. Deliverable: ADR-004.md in integration_concepts/adrs/.

title: ADR-003: Saga orchestrator
description: Decide the saga orchestration engine for complex multi-step flows (constitution, early mobilization, maturity renewal) described in docs 00 and 05. Conversation topics: Temporal vs Conductor vs Axon Framework vs rolling a custom orchestrator on top of the message broker; durable execution vs explicit state machines; how the orchestrator holds saga state and drives compensations; operational footprint and observability integration (doc 06). Deliverable: ADR-003.md in integration_concepts/adrs/.

title: ADR-002: Schema format and registry
description: Decide the serialization format and schema registry for all integration events. Doc 04 and 09 name Avro and Protobuf as candidates alongside a schema registry, but the choice is not made. Conversation topics: Avro vs Protobuf vs JSON Schema — compatibility rules, tooling, language support; Confluent Schema Registry vs AWS Glue Schema Registry vs Apicurio; forward/backward/full compatibility strategies tied to doc 09 evolution patterns; impact on the event catalog (doc 08). Deliverable: ADR-002.md in integration_concepts/adrs/.

title: ADR-001: Event backbone — message broker choice
description: Decide which message broker to use as the event backbone. The integration_concepts series assumes Kafka in a greenfield context (doc 00, 04), but the decision must be explicit and justified. Conversation topics: Kafka vs Pulsar vs RabbitMQ (streams mode) vs NATS JetStream; durability guarantees; topic compaction and retention for event sourcing; operational complexity in a Portuguese banking context; managed vs self-hosted. Deliverable: ADR-001.md in integration_concepts/adrs/.
